policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'began to speak unto them in parables' renders either verb; λαλεῖν and λέγειν are both idiomatically 'speak' with ἐν παραβολαῖς, and no note bears on it.
Word order only; English 'A man planted a vineyard' fixes subject-verb order regardless of the Greek sequence.
ASV reads 'of the fruits of the vineyard' — plural τῶν καρπῶν, not the singular τοῦ καρποῦ ('of the fruit').
ASV 'And they took him' fits either connective: καί with an implicit subject and οἱ δέ both come into English as 'And they', the pronoun being required by English syntax.
ASV has only 'him they wounded in the head, and handled shamefully' — no rendering of λιθοβολήσαντες ('having stoned'), which the RP addition would require.
ἐκεφαλίωσαν and ἐκεφαλαίωσαν are spelling variants of the same verb; both yield ASV 'wounded in the head'.

ASV 'and handled shamefully' has no verb of sending, so the RP ἀπέστειλαν ἠτιμωμένον ('sent away shamefully handled') is excluded; ἠτίμασαν and ἠτίμησαν are alternative aorist forms of one verb and English cannot separate them.
ASV 12:5 reads simply 'And he sent another' — no 'again' answering RP's added πάλιν (contrast 12:4, where ASV does render πάλιν as 'And again he sent').
οὕς μέν … οὕς δέ and τούς μέν … τούς δέ are equivalent correlatives; both give ASV 'beating some, and killing some'.

ASV 'He had yet one, a beloved son: he sent him last' uses a finite verb plus a second clause, excluding RP's participial ἔχων with its added καί ('sent him also'); the base and r01 are the same wording and English cannot separate them.
Word order only; ASV 'he sent him last unto them' is the natural English of either sequence.
Word order and aorist spelling (εἶπαν/εἶπον) only; ASV 'said among themselves' is neutral.
The variants differ in word order and in whether the pronoun object is repeated; English requires 'him' with both verbs in 'killed him, and cast him forth' either way.
ASV reads 'What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do?' — 'therefore' renders the οὖν that the base lacks.
ASV 'And when they were come, they say unto him' fits καί or οἱ δέ alike; the English subject pronoun is required in either case.
Word order only; 'to give tribute unto Caesar' is fixed by English syntax.

ASV reads 'And Jesus said unto them' with no rendering of ἀποκριθείς; the RP reading would give 'And Jesus answering said', a participle the ASV renders explicitly where it stands (cf. its practice elsewhere in this chapter).
ASV 'said unto them' renders the dative αὐτοῖς, which the WH reading omits.
Word order only; English 'Render unto Caesar the things that are Caesar's' must place the imperative first whichever Greek order stood.
ASV 'they marvelled greatly at him' renders the intensive compound ἐξεθαύμαζον; the simple ἐθαύμαζον/ἐθαύμασαν would give only 'marvelled'.
Imperfect against aorist of the same verb; ASV 'and they asked him, saying' does not distinguish the aspects here.
ASV reads 'and leave no child' — singular τέκνον, not the plural τέκνα of the Treg/RP reading.
ASV 'should take his wife' supplies the possessive that English idiom requires for the articular τὴν γυναῖκα, so it does not show whether αὐτοῦ stood in the Greek.
ASV 'and died, leaving no seed behind him' renders a negated participle (μὴ καταλιπών); the RP reading is a finite clause with emphatic subject, 'and neither did he himself leave seed'.
ASV reads only 'and the seven left no seed' — no rendering of RP's ἔλαβον αὐτήν ('the seven took her, and').
Adverbial ἔσχατον and predicative ἐσχάτη both come into English as 'Last of all'; the ASV wording does not show which stood.
Word order only; 'the woman also died' is the English of either sequence.
ASV reads 'In the resurrection whose wife shall she be of them?' with no rendering of ὅταν ἀναστῶσιν ('when they shall rise').
ASV 'Jesus said unto them' renders a bare verb of speaking; RP's καὶ ἀποκριθείς … εἶπεν would give 'And Jesus answering said', neither the 'And' nor the 'answering' appearing in the ASV.
γαμίζονται and γαμίσκονται are equivalent forms; both give ASV 'are given in marriage'.
Presence of the Greek article before ἄγγελοι; ASV 'as angels in heaven' does not register it.
ASV 'how God spake unto him' renders πῶς or ὡς equally; both are standard as 'how' in this indirect clause.
The candidates differ only in the Greek articles before θεός; ASV's 'the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob' supplies English articles required by the construction and does not register the Greek.
Article before θεός only; ASV 'He is not the God of the dead' would read the same either way.
ASV reads 'but of the living', carrying 'God' over by ellipsis as the base ἀλλὰ ζώντων does; the RP reading repeats θεός and would give 'but the God of the living'.
ASV 'ye do greatly err' has no 'therefore' answering the οὖν of the Treg/RP reading.
ASV reads 'and knowing that he had answered them well' — εἰδώς ('knowing'), not ἰδών ('seeing').
Word order only; 'he had answered them well' is fixed by English.
Word order only; ASV 'What commandment is the first of all?' is the English of either sequence.
ASV reads 'Jesus answered' with no indirect object; the Treg and RP readings add αὐτῷ, which would give 'answered him'.
ASV 'The first is, Hear, O Israel' has no rendering of RP's πάντων τῶν ἐντολῶν ('the first of all the commandments').
Presence of the Greek article only; ASV 'with all thy heart' is unaffected.
ASV ends 12:30 at 'with all thy strength' and begins 12:31 'The second is this' — no rendering of the added αὕτη πρώτη ἐντολή ('this is the first commandment').
ASV 'The second is this' contains nothing for ὁμοία ('like unto it') or for RP's leading καί.
ASV 12:32 opens 'And the scribe said unto him' and continues 'and there is none other but he' — the connective καί that WH omits is rendered.
Presence of the Greek article only; ASV 'with all the heart' is unaffected.
ASV lists three members — 'with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the strength' — with no 'and with all the soul' for the Treg/RP addition.
περισσότερον and πλεῖον are synonymous comparatives; both give ASV 'is much more than'.
ASV 'when Jesus saw that he answered discreetly' collapses the proleptic αὐτόν into the subordinate clause, as English idiom does, so it cannot show whether the pronoun stood.
Word order only; 'the Christ is the son of David' is fixed by English.
ASV 'David himself said in the Holy Spirit' has no 'for' answering the γάρ of the Treg/RP reading.
Presence of the Greek articles only; ASV 'in the Holy Spirit' reads the same either way.
ASV reads 'The Lord said unto my Lord' — the aorist εἶπεν; the historic present λέγει would be rendered 'saith', as the ASV consistently does elsewhere.
Article before κύριος only; ASV 'The Lord said' is unaffected.
κάθου and κάθισον are both imperatives of sitting; ASV 'Sit thou on my right hand' does not distinguish them.
ASV's text reads 'the footstool of thy feet' (ὑποπόδιον), and its note mapped here — 'Some ancient authorities read underneath thy feet' — assigns ὑποκάτω to the margin.
ASV 'David himself calleth him Lord' has no 'therefore' answering RP's added οὖν.
Word order only; 'whence is he his son?' is fixed by English.
ASV 'And in his teaching he said, Beware' has no indirect object, excluding RP's ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ('said unto them'); the base and r01 are the same wording and English cannot separate them.
ASV reads 'And he sat down over against the treasury' with a pronoun subject; RP's added ὁ Ἰησοῦς would give the name, as the ASV renders it wherever it stands.
κατέναντι and ἀπέναντι are synonymous; both give ASV 'over against'.
ASV 'and said unto them' renders the aorist εἶπεν; the historic present λέγει would be 'saith', the ASV's regular rendering.
ASV 'This poor widow cast in more than all' is a simple past for the aorist ἔβαλεν; the perfect βέβληκεν would be rendered 'hath cast in'.
